Red Pozole

Served at: Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe

Serves 8Prep 30 minCook 2 hr 30 min

Red Pozole is a traditional Mexican stew made with hominy, pork, and a rich red chili broth. It is commonly served during the Feast of Our Lady of Guadalupe on December 12th, a significant religious and cultural celebration in Mexico, symbolizing community and faith.

Ingredients

  • 2 pounds (900 g) pork shoulder, cut into chunks
  • 1 pound (450 g) pork ribs
  • 1 large white onion, halved
  • 6 cloves garlic, peeled
  • 2 teaspoons salt, plus more to taste
  • 8 cups (1.9 L) water
  • 2 cans (15 oz/425 g each) white hominy, drained and rinsed
  • 6 dried guajillo chilies, stemmed and seeded
  • 3 dried ancho chilies, stemmed and seeded
  • 1 teaspoon dried oregano
  • 1 teaspoon ground cumin
  • 1/2 teaspoon black pepper
  • 2 tablespoons vegetable oil
  • Garnishes: shredded cabbage, sliced radishes, chopped white onion, lime wedges, dried oregano, tostadas or tortilla chips

Method

  1. Place pork shoulder, pork ribs, onion halves, garlic cloves, salt, and water in a large pot and bring to a boil.
  2. Reduce heat and simmer uncovered for about 1.5 to 2 hours until pork is tender.
  3. Remove pork and set aside to cool. Strain broth and return to pot.
  4. While pork cooks, toast guajillo and ancho chilies in a dry skillet over medium heat for 1-2 minutes until fragrant, being careful not to burn them.
  5. Soak toasted chilies in hot water for 20 minutes until softened.
  6. Blend soaked chilies with 1 cup (240 ml) of the soaking water until smooth.
  7. Heat vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook chili sauce for 5 minutes, stirring frequently.
  8. Add chili sauce to the broth and stir in oregano, cumin, and black pepper.
  9. Shred cooled pork and add it back to the pot along with the drained hominy.
  10. Simmer the pozole for another 30 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
  11. Adjust salt to taste.
  12. Serve hot with garnishes such as shredded cabbage, radishes, onion, lime wedges, oregano, and tostadas or tortilla chips.

Tips

  • For a spicier pozole, add a few dried arbol chilies to the chili blend.
  • Hominy can be found canned or dried; if using dried, soak and cook it beforehand according to package instructions.
  • Leftover pozole tastes even better the next day as flavors deepen.
